sections.overview: Lycia lapponaria is a geometrid moth of cool upland moors; in Britain it is restricted to damp moorland in central and northern Scotland.
sections.identification: Males have whitish forewings marked in black and red markings on the thorax and abdomen, while females are wingless.
sections.habitat: In its British range it inhabits damp moorland, where bog myrtle and heathers grow.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on several moorland plants, including bog myrtle, heather and bilberry.
sections.behavior: Adults emerge in spring; the wingless female cannot fly, unlike the male.
sections.reproduction: The pupa overwinters, and the caterpillars feed during summer on their host plants.
sections.ecology: A Scottish site assessment describes this moth as localised and dependent on bogs that sustain its larval food plants.
sections.conservation: The same assessment notes its localised British distribution, but it is an older site review rather than a current global Red List assessment.
